messages.author: c7c54e822c5daae0
messages.subject: Warning interpretation
parts:
Hi,

I ran the GGIR with thresholds and criteria's and I got the following warning in R.

In g.report.part4(datadir = datadir, metadatadir = metadatadir,  : NAs introduced by coercion

I saw that in the summary file "part4_nightsummary_sleep_cleaned", the variable nonwear_perc_spt (Non-wear percentage during the spt hours of this day) has many NA's. Why is that so? How should I interpret this? Do I need to be wary about this warning?

Kind regards,
Parneet

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Warning interpretation
parts:
These values are copied from the GGIR part 5 output. It is probably best to first investigate whether nonwear_perc_spt is available and plausible in the part 5 csv reports. Can you check?
Vincent

Hi Vincent,

nonwear_perc_spt  is available in this file. The participants were asked to wear the monitors overnight. May be some participants did not follow that instruction and because of that non wear during the sleep period can be plausible. 
There is another problem with the day summary file (example row 2 and 3) have different window numbers but the calendar date is the same for them. I don't understand why this should happen. This is happening across all the studies that I'm analysing the AG monitors for using GGIR.
I have attached the day summary file from part 5 too.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Warning interpretation
parts:
See https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#waking-waking-or-24-hour-time-use-analysis
These are the timewindows defined in part 5, either based on midnight-midnight days or based on wakingup-wakingup (WW) windows. I called it window number instead of day number to emphasize that these are time windows that typically overlap with two calendar days.

Vincent
